questions.question: Write the seven levels of the classification hierarchy in order from largest to smallest, and state two things that change as you move down the hierarchy.
questions.expected_answer: Kingdom, Phylum (Division for plants), Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. Moving down, each group contains fewer kinds of organisms, and the organisms in each group share more characteristics and are more closely related.

questions.question: Define a species. State the rules for writing a scientific name, using the lion as an example, and give two advantages of scientific names over common names.
questions.expected_answer: A species is a group of organisms that can breed with each other and produce fertile offspring. A scientific name has two parts (binomial nomenclature): the genus with a capital letter and the species name with a small letter, printed in italics or underlined when handwritten: Panthera leo. Advantages: the name is the same in every country and language, so it avoids confusion (lion, ingonyama, tau, leeu); each name refers to only one species, while common names can refer to different organisms in different places; the genus shows relationships.

questions.question: Lion: Animals, Chordata, Mammalia, Carnivora, Felidae, Panthera, leo. Leopard: same but species pardus. Human: Animals, Chordata, Mammalia, Primates, Hominidae, Homo, sapiens. Which two are more closely related, and how do you know?
questions.expected_answer: The lion and leopard are more closely related because they share every level down to genus (Panthera), whereas the lion and human share levels only down to class (Mammalia). The lower the level two organisms share, the more closely related they are.
